text:
Jules: Heads-up — OrchidBank POC reporting intermittent spikes in tail latency and a few 429s during peak demo runs. They said response sometimes takes 3–5s and occasionally gets a 429 mid-stream. Can SE/SRE swarm?
Ravi: On it. Which model and plan are they using? Any rate-limit headers in the logs?
Jules: They're on hosted xlarge-v1, default concurrency. Customer pasted snippet: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 60\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 48\n\n...streaming tokens start then 429 after 2s`
Tess: Remaining=0 indicates per-minute seat concurrency exhaustion. Hosted enforces soft concurrency and token-rate limits to protect capacity. Do we have their seat id to check quota?
Jules: Seat is seat-ORCH-77. I forwarded logs to debug@redwood.
ops-bot: [alert] orchidbank-poc: tail_95p=4.9s tail_99p=7.2s rate_limit_trips=6 last_1h concurrency_spikes=14
Anika: Tail looks bad. Two likely causes: 1) batching/continuous-batcher holding for fill threshold, 2) KV/prefix cache misses forcing extra compute before first tokens. Also streaming can interact with batching windows.
Ravi: Does streaming increase wait? I thought streaming sends first token quickly.
Anika: If server waits for batch to fill with streaming requests, first token waits. With streaming enabled but batch windows set to accumulate, you can see delay before first byte.
Tess: Check their calls for `session_id` or per-request GUID in prompt — that destroys KV reuse. Ask them if they include variable metadata in prompts.
Jules: They do include `request_id` and timestamp in the prefix.
Ravi: Okay that's a big hit on cache. Recommend replacing dynamic bits with placeholders and pass metadata in a structured field.
Marta: Security question came up too — they want confirmation hosted never persists unencrypted prompt text outside ephemeral compute and that any HSM/KMS use is FIPS validated. I'll draft a short answer.
Jules: Draft would be great. Meanwhile SRE, can you throttle bump or a temporary rate-lift for this POC?
Tess: We can do a temporary quota increase for their seat and a short routing change to low-latency lane. I'll open ticket #SVC-9043. Temporary uplift until 2390016180. Note: this buys time but doesn't fix root cause.
Ravi: Actions for customer: 1) remove dynamic tokens from prompt prefix, 2) run a 20-request warmup using a stable prefix, 3) disable heavy per-request metadata in-text, 4) switch streaming to false for initial warmup.
Jules: Customer worried about billing if they run warmup. Any credits?
sales-ops-bot: [note] Submitted one-off credit request SO-4421 for OrchidBank — pending approval.
Anika: Also check model variant — if they moved from a quantized xlarge-q to xlarge-v1 we may see longer kernel init. Ask which variant.
Jules: Confirmed: they recently pointed to `xlarge-v1` (non-quantized) after we suggested better quality.
Tess: That explains some CPU/GPU kernel overhead. For hosted, recommend `xlarge-q` for lower latency during POCs or we can pin a faster serving variant.
Marta: Security draft: "Hosted compute encrypts data at rest and in transit; keys are managed by customer KMS when using Dedicated; hosted offers envelope encryption and keys in HSM. No plaintext keys stored. We can provide SOC2 artifacts and a KMS diagram." I'll send via email.
Ravi: I'm going to DM them a minimal prompt template and a tiny warmup script:```\n# warmup (bash)\nfor i in $(seq 1 20); do\n  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \\n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_TOKEN" \\n    -H "X-Redwood-Serve: low-latency" \\n    -d '{"model":"xlarge-q","prompt":"<<STABLE_PREFIX>> test"}'\ndone\n``` 
Jules: Nice. Also ask them to report whether 429s include `Retry-After` headers; if so we can tune client backoff to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Tess: I'll also enable per-seat circuit protection logging so we can correlate: ticket #LOG-2992. Meanwhile I'll monitor the seat metrics after warmup.
Anika: One more tip: if they rely on streamed partial outputs for UI, consider using a short non-streaming initial call to prime KV and then use streaming for follow-ups. That tends to reduce first-token lag.
Jules: I'll consolidate and send the plan: prompt template + warmup + variant suggestion + expect credit and temporary quota bump.
Ravi: I'll follow up with a short example patch to their template to remove `timestamp` and `request_id` and show how to pass them as headers.
Marta: Security docs will be in your inbox in ~30m.
Tess: Monitoring now — will post updates.
ops-bot: [update] orchidbank-poc: prefill_cache_miss=68% post_warmup_check_pending routing_override=SVC-9043 credits_pending=SO-4421
Jules: Thanks team — I'll message the customer and schedule a 30-min repro window. :thumbsup:
